title: lifespan-extract paper record
description: One file = one paper. A paper contributes one experiment entry per (organism, intervention) pair, so multi-organism papers yield multiple entries in experiments[]. Claim fields carry provenance; paper metadata is flat because it comes from the ingest API rather than the prose.

schema_version.description: Semver of the schema this record was written against. Extraction is idempotent per (paper, schema_version). Deliberately a pattern rather than a const: additive releases stay backward compatible, so an older record still validates.

paper.description: Bibliographic identity. Flat values: these come from PubMed/bioRxiv metadata, not from extracted prose, so they carry no source_quote.

doi.description: Canonical DOI, lowercase. Dedup key for preprint/publication pairs.

year.description: Publication year (preprint posting year for unpublished preprints).

source.description: Ingest origin. PMC open-access full text is not a separate source: it is source=pubmed with extracted_from=full_text on the claims. Phase 1 clients conform to this enum, not the reverse.

pmid.description: PubMed ID where one exists. null for preprints not yet indexed.

experiments.description: One entry per (organism, intervention) pair reported in the paper.

confidence.description: Categorical, not numeric: the gold set is labeled by a human, and humans cannot produce calibrated probabilities. Eval comparison is exact-match on the category.

extracted_from.description: Which text the claim was read from. Abstract-only extractions are expected to yield not_reported more often, especially for sex.

provenance.description: Provenance keys shared by every claim wrapper. Composed via allOf; wrappers add their own typed `value`.

source_quote.description: Verbatim sentence from the paper supporting the value. null only when there is nothing to quote, i.e. the value is null or not_reported.

value.description: MVP filters cover the two named organisms. `other` exists so gold-set papers outside scope (e.g. the Colman 2009 / Mattison 2012 macaque pair) can be labeled truthfully rather than forced into a wrong bucket.
not_reported is a real answer, not a gap. Sex is often buried in methods and must come back not_reported from abstract-only extraction.
no_effect must survive evasive phrasing ("did not significantly alter") without being coerced into a weak increase.
Free text. null means not reported. Open-vocabulary fields use null rather than the string "not_reported" so they never collide with a real value.
null means not reported. Never a sentinel number: -1 is a legitimate percentage change.

String, because papers report thresholds rather than numbers: "< 0.001" is not parseable as a float without losing the inequality. null means not reported; a bare "n.s." is recorded as null with lifespan_effect.direction = no_effect.

experiment.description: One (organism, intervention) pair. Required fields are the ones that make a record meaningful at all; everything else is optional and nullable.

experiment_id.description: Stable identity for the API and for eval alignment. Convention: <first-author-year>-<organism-slug>-<agent-slug>[-<n>], all lowercase ASCII, hyphen-separated; the trailing -<n> disambiguates repeat (organism, agent) pairs within one paper. Assigned by hand in data/gold/; generated deterministically from the same convention in Phase 2. Flat, not a claim wrapper: it is derived identity, not something quoted from the paper.

strain.description: Open vocabulary (N2, UM-HET3, C57BL/6). Uses the literal string "not_reported" when absent, matching the categorical convention for strain-like fields.

sample_size.description: Number of animals in the treated cohort, where reported.

agent.description: Name of the compound, gene, or regimen as reported. Normalization is a later phase.

age_at_start.description: As reported, units included ("600 days", "day 1 of adulthood"). Free text in v0: units are not consistent enough across organisms to normalize yet.

mechanism.description: Proposed mechanism as stated by the authors, not inferred. Backs the ?mechanism= API filter.

median_change_pct.description: Percent change in MEDIAN lifespan vs control. Kept structurally distinct from mean_change_pct and max_change_pct: conflating them is a known failure mode. null if the paper reports only a mean — never substitute one statistic for the other.

mean_change_pct.description: Percent change in MEAN lifespan (life expectancy) vs control. Added in v0.2.0: mouse papers such as Harrison 2009 report a mean/life-expectancy change with no pooled median percentage, which previously forced a choice between losing the number and misfiling it as median.

max_change_pct.description: Percent change in MAXIMUM lifespan vs control.

notes.description: Free-text labeller commentary. Flat, not a claim wrapper: it is human annotation, not something extracted and quoted from the paper, so it carries no provenance and is never scored in evals. Destination for content that must not become a record of its own — cohorts with no reported effect size (interim analyses), and speculative mechanisms raised in the discussion rather than stated as the mechanism of action. null when there is nothing to say.
